headline: Benchmarking segmentation and synthetic ground truth for 3D tissue and organoid imaging
label: Spatial Omics Tissue Analysis
summary: Recent preprints benchmark segmentation on Xenium and CODEX data and introduce ground-truth-free and synthetic validation for tissue imaging.
synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative image analysis in tissue geometry, where segmentation accuracy and reconstruction fidelity bound what can be measured. Two items benchmark segmentation directly: CRISP compares five algorithms across ten mouse tissues on Xenium spatial transcriptomics using a ground-truth-free purity metric, and a separate evaluation tests Cellpose-SAM, microSAM, CellSAM, Mesmer and InstanSeg on live microscopy and CODEX spatial-omics data. Other items address ground truth and reconstruction: a parametric physics-based framework generates 3D organoid fluorescence images with exact cell and nucleus masks, and a volume electron microscopy pipeline segments gold nanoparticles and cells in SBF-SEM tumor spheroids. ToFiE reconstructs dense 3D fiber networks from microscopy, and LEAO improves aberration estimation more than sixfold for intravital fluorescence imaging. The new elements are the ground-truth-free metric and synthetic ground truth; the work is primarily method development and benchmarking rather than biological conclusions.
